projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

body.p: I am thankful my mind hath been often engaged in near sympathy with thee under my late arduous embassy, which has often appraised a trying path, but I find it best to endeavor to do what little I can, if I can only obtain a single might to cast into the treasury. We have deep wading sometimes, but it is a mercy inexpressible when made willing to suffer with the seed, for as we abide faithful, when it reigns, we shall reign also. Many are the fare, inexperienced, uninformed youths in the land of Carolina, which we entered 5 or 6 weeks ago, & perhaps more, after taking meetings through the back parts of Virginia. And since we arrived at New Garden, have performed a visit in company with our dear Friend John Wishham to thee families of Friends of New Garden particular meeting, which we accomplished the day before yesterday–about 80 in numbers– and this day have attended the quarterly meeting for New Gardens held at Deep River. I trust the great shepherd of Israel was with us, for which favor I desired to bow as in my first door for the work is altogether his-the power and the glory.

Dear Hannah, pray for me, that I may use the field and also hardness as a good soldier. I believe I have felt
my heart bound to the precious immortal cause but and as long as our blessed captain & leader goeth before and salutes his little flocks with the endeared language. Be of good Christ, and drawing with the cords of his love. May we not run after him and hopest in the accomplishment of the warfare. Yet my cup overflow. Oh, may they be sure and in the way of holiness too–and the excellency of the creator always in the dust. I gave a hint respecting the dear young people who labor under many & great disadvantages, and yet the forming hand is laid upon some of them who are acquainted with retirement and near stillness. My prayers are for them that they may move in a holy solidity, attending to the tender [?] the Lord hath been pleased to rouse in their minds then will that gracious declaration be fulfilled in them, their people have I formed for myself, and they shall show forth my praise–I feel nearly for my dear Friends with you and in my own neighborhood. I did believe the Lord had driven in both places and by his holy quickening life remain also afresh for service. I desire they, with myself, may walk worthy of all his blessings & favor, which to my humbling admission have been mystified.

And now dear Friend,
being acquainted with thy diffident mind I instruct thee not to be cast down when the true bread is scarce, and weakness upon thy loins. And even permitted to feel as though the divine presence was beheld, for the Lord is the strength of his people, & his ear is open to their praying and their gracious words proceeding out of his mouth, that man shall not live by bread alone but by every word proceeding from the mouth of God. And in there dispensations how can close the immortal life in us is nurtured. I know I am writing to one of longer experience than myself, though I am sure my sympathy has been often great with thee, when thou hast been ready to utter–is there any savior like unto my savior? May a holy tranquility rest upon thy mind, and heart. Hannah, be encouraged to sit down with the little flock under thy prayers, for the good will of him that dwells in the bush is near and watches over you to do your good.

I have been filling up my time in various services. Since coming the Carolina have visited all the meetings of Cane Creek greater & most belonging to new garden. In a day or two expect to move forward in company with dear John Wisham and my beloved companion James Emlen towards Westfield
